:::{#def-huffman-code}
#### Huffman code

Let $X$ be a [discrete random variable](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-discrete-rv) that takes $n \ge 2$ values,
with [probability mass function](https://morrison-lab.github.io/pds/random-variables.html#def-pmf) $p$.
A **Huffman code** for $X$ is a [binary code](source-coding.qmd#def-code) built in three steps:

1. Start with $n$ nodes, one for each value $x$, with weight $p(x)$.
2. Repeat $n - 1$ times:
   take two nodes of the smallest weights,
   make them the two children of a new node whose weight is the sum of theirs,
   and label the edge to one child $0$ and the edge to the other child $1$.
3. Give each value $x$ the codeword made of the labels on the path from the last node down to the node for $x$.

Ties between nodes of equal weight may be broken in any way,
so a random variable can have several Huffman codes.

:::
